For example, if a human subject were to touch SCP-9024 with a stick, both the human and the stick would get absorbed by SCP-9024.

SCP-9025-2 is a pocket dimension located in ████████ Park in ████████, ███ ████. The pocket dimension is abstractly circular, with an average radius of 2.23 miles, and is surrounded on all sides by thick foliage. Though it is suspected that this was not always the case, the sky in SCP-9025-2 is dark red, as is all light that comes from its frequently overcast sky.

SCP-9025-2 was created by a group of anartists taking the form of a punk/rock band named "The Neverlanders". Though this is unconfirmed, it is suspected that the keyboard player of the band, Stacy Femcop AKA Archer Federa-Lespit, was responsible for the creation of SCP-9025-2, and the rites that became necessary to access it.

SCP-9026 is a three-story German-style American suburban home containing a spatio-temporal Richards-Keeley fractal structure. Its original owner, [NAME REDACTED FOR PRIVACY], operated a home therapy clinic for those with mild to moderate PTSD.

SCP-9026‘s anomalous properties manifest whenever an individual (hereby referred to as the "patient") opens the front door to the house. The house will take on the appearance of significant locations within the patient‘s memory, most often that of a childhood home. Though no other living individuals will be present, remnants of their activity are apparent throughout the house.

SCP-9027 is the designation for a behavioral pattern presented by individuals who seemingly have no connection with one another. Individuals affected by SCP-9027, henceforth designated SCP-9027-1, undergo two stages of deterioration.
• Stage 1: Initially, SCP-9027-1 instances undergo a process of isolation, gradually reducing their interaction with other individuals until it becomes nearly nonexistent. Additionally, all known instances of SCP-9027-1 begin to consider themselves "already deceased" and claim they no longer have any desire or motivation to participate in any kind of activity, including those that they formerly enjoyed.
To the Fate of the Faithful

SCP-9028 is an anomalous pir. Zoroastrian Pilgrimage site, translated from Persian (پیر). For clarity, all Persian and Avestan words have been Romanized unless specified. found within the Shekaft-e Yazdan cave near the village Zarju, Iran.. Population approx. 70. While not one of the six most holy pilgrimage sites of the Yazd region, Zoroastrian legend holds that Shekaft-e Yazdan was used to hide the sacred flame during various Hellenistic and Sassanian conflicts and is still a popular location for worship. Ingress to the cave which houses SCP-9028 provides some challenge due to altitude and entrance formation, while SCP-9028 itself is only accessible to visitors via ritualistic behaviors hereafter referred to as Protocol Mithra..

The designation 'SCP-9029' refers to an anomalous colony of leafcutter ants, located in a 5km wide forested zone in Southern Texas. While SCP-9029 mostly resembles a mature colony of Atta mexicana, workers of SCP-9029, referred to hereby as SCP-9029-1, have never been seen cutting or consuming any type of leaf. SCP-9029 as a colony also harbours an abnormal ratio of workers to majors, with over 40 percent of the colonies estimated population being composed of majors.

SCP-9030 is a phenomenon affecting seemingly random pieces of media primarily in North America. SCP-9030 will “infest” a piece of media and change its narrative. These changes largely consist of the additions of pigs and their subsequent deaths. These deaths are usually implied to be incredibly violent, but are rarely described or seen. Characters within the narrative do not react to these deaths or other changes within the narrative in any meaningful way. If changes to the narrative are consistent with the original tone, plot, and characterization, they are reacted to accordingly.

SCP-9030 is believed to have existed within several narratives before becoming anomalous.

SCP-9031 is contained at Site-███, sublevel 14, within a purpose-built vacuum-sealed chamber (designated Chamber 9031-Alpha). The threshold aperture is to be enclosed in a reinforced steel housing bolted to a seismically isolated platform. The chamber is to be maintained at negative pressure relative to the surrounding corridor to prevent atmospheric exchange with SCP-9031-A.

No personnel may enter SCP-9031-A without written authorization from two Level-2 researchers. Exploration teams are to remain tethered at all times via magnetically anchored filament cable rated to 12 kN. Untethered entry is prohibited under all circumstances. Excursion time within SCP-9031-A to be no greater than 8 hours.

SCP-9032 is a phenomenon that occurs on individuals (designated SCP-9032-1) that are unable to perceive time normally. SCP-9032-1 entities are typically:
• Largely inaccurate in perceiving the time duration of an event, a thought, or a physical process. Those can include daily activities such as eating, sleeping, and talking, as well as academic or professional activities. Still, the latter is uncommon due to the impact this trait has on their careers.
• The margins of said inaccuracy range from 0.1% (1ms / second) to 50% (0.5s / second).
• This trait must not be a result of other pre-existing conditions (disease, trauma, etc.).

SCP-9033 is the procedure in which SCP objects are sorted in the database. Certain anomalies are effected by attempts to categorise and describe them, which therefore necessitates certain SCP slots being reserved or repurposed for appropriate containment. In anomalies where such procedures aren't applicable, it has been found that SCP's with random designations have been subject to incidents such as containment breaches, damage, loss, and unintended neutralisation at a higher rate than those with intentional designations. The reason for this is unknown.
There's A Man-Shaped Hole in God's Heart

The following file is classified at Level-5 Clearance on orders from the O5 Council. Unauthorized access is strictly forbidden. Any attempt to access the file without proper clearance will result in immediate termination.

SCP-9035 designates "Foundationland", the official SCP Foundation theme park, located in Fukuoka, Japan, and all anomalies contained within.

The park include thrill rides, dark rides, eateries, mascot meet-and-greets, and educational facilities—all assisted by, or created with anomalies. Foundationland receives 18.25 million visitors annually, and generates approximately ¥5 trillion per year ($32.5 billion).

SCP-9035 was created in response to the booming interest in the SCP Foundation since Veilfall, and was developed in collaboration with the Department of Entertainment, the SCP Foundation's Japanese branch, and the Japan Tourism Agency, and is operated entirely by Foundation personnel.

SCP-9036 is a phenomenon in which the SCP Foundation functions more efficiently and cohesively than is statistically plausible for such an organization. This includes but is not limited to appropriation of resources and personnel, bureaucratic organization, lack of corruption, lack of factionalism, response to crises (both active and proactive), ability to remain in good standing with and procure funding from numerous governments all around the world, and general efficacy of strategies devised by administrative personnel.

SCP-9036 is believed to be endemic to the SCP Foundation.

SCP-9037 is partially an ideological complex existing within the noosphere (realm of human thought). SCP-9037’s complex is primarily constructed of anti-noospheric (realm outside of human thought) content, possibly of an alternate reality. This composition makes SCP-9037 incredibly unstable, as it contains abnormal and incompatible conceptual constructs. If completely isolated, SCP-9037 would collapse and release mass amounts of anomalous structures into the physical or metaphysical world. SCP-9037 can gain noospheric proximity to ideological structures by associating itself closer to the target concept.

SCP-9037 appears to be a mixture of various objects constantly in a volatile flux. The total mass of SCP-9037 takes up 6 spatial dimensions.

SCP-9038 refers to a volume of thaumaturgically engineered space. SCP-9038 originated from the research of a hypothesis that not all ectoentropic anomalies are actually ectoentropic; that some of them do not create (or eliminate) mass and energy from nowhere, but transfer mass and energy from (or to) another location within the universe and then transform them into the intended object.

Foundation cosmology research has proven that, given the large amount of matter generated by all ectoentropic anomalies known to humanity thus far, the observable universe should have shown perceptible changes over the eons due to the change of its total mass.

SCP-9039 refers to a true crime podcast colloquially referred to as "A Perfect Crime Podcast", which covers murders while adding an often inaccurate paranormal tinge. Episodes of the Perfect Crime Podcast have been discovered in numerous websites, with the majority of sightings being on the Parawatch Wiki forums (See addendum 1). Attempts to trace the IP address of the podcast's host have so far been unsuccessful. There is few information available on the host—if such a host even exists—apart from the fact that they are female and have been spotted under the online alias “A_Perfect_Podcast” and variations of such.

SCP-9040 is the collective designation for a population of Blattella germanica: individually designated SCP-9040-01 through SCP-9040-53. Instances exhibit sapience, fluent vocal speech, anthropomorphic behavior, and significantly extended lifespans. All wear garments consistent with late-18th century European maritime fashion, typically accessorized with sewing needles in place of swords and miniature firecrackers in place of pistols.
”The lost seeker found traces of truth in the mist. And so, he set off for the material world.”
SCP-9042 denotes the entirety of the Sol stellar system, excluding the Sun and Earth, following the effects of the Cascade Event.

SCP-9043 is a pair of socks, featuring a light brown and navy blue striped pattern.

Any static electricity SCP-9043 accumulates can only be released by an electrostatic discharge; all other methods fail. The anomaly demonstrates greater elasticity than what its composition should allow. Attempts to trace SCP-9043's origins beyond the circumstances surrounding its acquisition have failed (See — History.)
A House with People in it

SCP-9044 is a hallway. SCP-9044 is located inside of a suburban home located at 8541 ███████ Lane, Virginia. The end of SCP-9044 has not yet been reached. Opening the door located at the perceived end of SCP-9044 invariably reveals another room terminating in another door. Scratching sounds can be heard from other parts of the house.

SCP-9044 was first discovered following the disappearance of every member of the Lorey family, believed to have occurred during a housewarming party. All 27 attendees followed them in. Their vehicles remain parked outside.

Three months later, eleven residents in the neighborhood also went missing. The local police report suggested that they have moved.

SCP-9045 is an anomalous retrocausal phenomenon by which unknown individuals (SCP-9045-1) appear within media and documentation (such as newspapers, photographs, birth certificates, and marriage licenses). Despite their appearance being near-identical to known individuals, the identities of these instances cannot be corroborated or confirmed by anyone, beyond stating that they "look like someone they've seen before."

These unknown individuals (SCP-9045-1) manifest as depictions of those with all-encompassing secrets; specifically those requiring extensive deception, elaborate cover stories, and near-disassociation from one's personality to conceal long term.
These tasks take precedence over all other Foundation duties and personal responsibilities.

SCP-9047 is a male Cardigan Welsh corgi which is identical to any other dog of its breed, with the exception of its exceptional longevity and apparent total immunity to physical trauma and pathogens (whether anomalous or non-anomalous), rendering it incapable of carrying or transmitting any infectious agents. Besides this, SCP-9047 displays no unusual behavior, and exhibits standard behavioral responses to positive and negative stimuli—with the exception of exposure to pathogens or physical harm, which it simply ignores. SCP-9047 is described by Foundation personnel as having a calm, affectionate personality, and is usually referred to by its nickname "Craig" outside of official documentation.

SCP-9048 is the collective designation for SCP-9048-1, “The Banksworth Theatre”, and SCP-9048-2 instances, individuals who have previously been exposed to a performance within SCP-9048-1. Every year, within one week of May 1st, SCP-9048-1 will manifest and draw in an audience to watch the upcoming performance. This occurrence has been designated as the "Ouroboros Event".

Through interviews of SCP-9048-2 instances, it has been determined that the Ouroboros Event consists of a play adaptation of the Russian fairytale The Animals in the Pit, following the version written by Alexander Nikolaevich Afanasyev. A transcript of the Ouroboros Event along with Incident 99-X can be found in Document 99-X-THE_ANIMALS_IN_THE_PIT.

SCP-9049 is a limit on the total number of human teeth that can exist on Earth at any given time. The precise value of this limit is not known, though estimates have placed it at around 7.0*10¹². When the number of human teeth on Earth exceeds SCP-9049, no new teeth will develop; this affects the growth of deciduous and permanent teeth as well as all known anomalous dental sources. SCP-9049 was first reached on October 19th, 2049; the Total Tooth Count (TTC) did not dip below SCP-9049 until May 3rd, 2050, at which point the correlation between the TTC and the ongoing global dental catastrophe was discovered. The exact nature of SCP-9049 is not yet fully understood.

Over the past several months, a faction inside our organisation began to stray away from the foundational missions that were dictated by our founder. What was once ideological friction has escalated into an open insurrection and incursion. Their actions have already resulted in casualties, material losses, and the compromise of a few secure sites.

The group responsible believed that the Anomalous could be turned into a weapon, one for the betterment of mankind. When confronted, they chose violence over compliance. Never before has the Foundation witnessed the scale of internal aggression, as is seen here, since its ratification in 1901.

Let me be clear: this “affliction” is not an ally.

SCP-9051 is a 1 fluid ounce elliptical bottle labeled "Spa Therapy Shampoo". The fluid inside the bottle has been identified as identical to non-anomalous shampoo. The fluid within the bottle can be removed and used as shampoo. However, SCP-9051 can never be fully emptied.

When opened, SCP-9051 will also generate SCP-9051-A, an entity made out of same fluid inside SCP-9051 within a 3 meter spherical radius of its location. The entity is capable of emitting gurgling noises, but cannot move, speak or demonstrate any other indications of sapience. Anyone also in the 3 meter spherical radius with SCP-9051-A will report mild distress and headaches when hearing the gurgles emitted by the entity.

SCP-9052 refers to a week-long event of anomalous activity which took place at the gravesite of Zechariah Robinsons (PoI-9052-1). The gravestone of PoI-9052-1 will henceforth be referred to as SCP-9052-1. All anomalous activity at SCP-9052-1 took place over the time period of 1/22/201█ to 1/29/201█, periodically from 11:00 PM - 11:59 PM every day.

SCP-9053 designates an anomalous phenomenon affecting mannequins, dolls, and other imitations of humanity. These mannequins will often be observed engaging in behavior that suggests sapience and locomotion, often in a manner that is considered uncanny and threatening. All observed events have later been determined to have entirely mundane explanations, however the frequency at which these events occur still warrant investigation.
The Anatomy of a Dying Smile
Thank you to all my critters and vibe checkers, as always: P4TR1CK07, Anyar, AstralNavigator, ViciousSpirit, ThanTheDemoness, jswessler, SierraBlade220, Arcane_Treatise, Cdudeman123, Heck_Tech

SCP-9055 is a large, complex, subterranean structure located directly below Site-14.

SCP-9055 is potently antimemetically cloaked in its entirety, with only Class-Z Mnestics able to render it perceptible to sentient creatures. When others are made aware of SCP-9055, or have their attention drawn towards it in any way, they exhibit a profound disinterest and are unable to recall any data about it, including its existence in the first place.

The ‘top’ of SCP-9055 is approximately 150 metres below Site-14’s basement. The structure extends at least a further 450 metres downwards, but its exact depth is unknown.

Addendum 9055.1: Discovery

I found it whilst looking for a cure to this overdose.

SCP-9056 is an amorphous mass fluctuating between 1 and 2 meters in height which levitates approximately 1.5 meters off the ground at all times. Its surface constantly displays an ever-changing array of images, the meaning of which is currently unknown. The object is sentient and capable of telepathic communication within a range of 5 meters.

SCP-9057 is a phenomenon that interferes in the perception of an individual's speech. It does not have an effect on non-verbal methods of communication. Anyone hearing this altered speech will perceive it as uninteresting in both content and delivery. Due to this perception being subjective, different individuals will perceive this speech in different ways. Individuals afflicted with SCP-9057 are not affected in this way, but suffer from other effects, including:
• persistent, mild forgetfulness.
• general confusion in day-to-day life.
• sudden isolation due to others' avoidance of social interaction with them due to the anomaly's effects.

SCP-9058 is an adult male domestic cat; it weighs 4.9kg, has black fur, and is neutered. While SCP-9058 is apparently healthy and genetically and anatomically normal, it has not been observed to vocalize at all.

SCP-9058 is capable of walking directly through any closed door as though it were not present; doorways without an attached door are also traversable. SCP-9058 cannot voluntarily pass through a doorway if a door is present and open, but it can be carried or otherwise forced through.

When left to its own devices, SCP-9058 will enter a residential building and attempt to ingratiate itself with the occupant(s) through displays of affection and playfulness. If this is unsuccessful, SCP-9058 will leave and attempt again at a different building.

SCP-9059 is an event involving two human subjects, designated SCP-9059-FINDER and SCP-9059-SEEKER.

When the event begins, SCP-9059-FINDER will become aware that a single human tooth has spontaneously manifested in a hidden or difficult-to-access location within the room they are currently occupying. While facing the direction of the tooth, FINDER subjects will perceive it vividly, even if it should be obscured by closed eyelids or other objects. This typically causes feelings of confusion and distress, leading FINDER subjects to seek aid from nearby personnel while keeping the tooth out of their vision as much as possible.

Only one individual, the SCP-9059-SEEKER instance, can interact with the tooth while SCP-9059 is ongoing.

SCP-9060 refers to a viral cognitohazardous phenomenon that causes a person (designated SCP-9060-1) to enter a violent state when their full face is viewed by another human (designated SCP-9060-2), whether directly, via video recording, photography, or on social media platforms.

SCP-9060-1 instances will display signs of emotional distress, including crying, screaming and incoherent speech, as they pursue SCP-9060-2. Subjects will only move in a straight line toward their target, regardless of potential for physical damage, death, or further exposure. In this state, SCP-9060-1 instances display heightened speed and strength, running up to 100 km/h and lifting up to 200 kilograms.

SCP-9061 was a Charlie I class nuclear submarine, manufactured by the USSR at some point between 1967 and 1969. SCP-9061's hull was completely black, lacking any of the typical markings found on other vessels of the same class. SCP-9061 was capable of autonomous movement, as well as travelling at speeds and depths far greater than what its structure should have been capable of.

SCP-9061 would typically keep to depths between 800m and 1000m, making tracking difficult. However, it would occasionally surface to emit brief radio broadcasts in Russian, before submerging again. These broadcasts were seemingly random, and typically consisted of single words or short statements.

SCP-9062 is a cube-like structure, hypothesised to exist in a higher dimensional plane than our own. Its standard size is 9 x 9 x 9 metres, though has been observed to shrink to as small as 2 x 2 x 2 millimetres, and expand as large as 30 x 30 x 30 metres. There is no known upper or lower limits to how much it can alter its size.

SCP-9062 is capable of off-ground levitation - most often suspending itself in-place in the air as it changes its size - though typically rests on the ground. The reason for this is unknown; possibly as a method of conserving energy and/or to appear more "natural" within baseline reality.

Almost the entire surface of SCP-9062 is covered in prongs of uniform length.

SCP-9063 is a series of abnormal fatalities occurring in and around the unincorporated community of Pemberton, Texas. As of Foundation recording, no cause for these fatalities has been established, nor have the conditions for such an anomaly to occur been identified. As of writing, the last SCP-9063 incident occurred on October 20, 2024.

The population of Pemberton has decreased to 26 as of the 2020 US census. Independent Foundation figures predict population figures further decreasing, and a separate Foundation census in 2025 recorded 21 individuals remaining in the community. As such, containment of SCP-9063 is currently considered low priority.

SCP-9064 is Foundation-made antimemetic concept "UNDERKILL" (AM-68-1).

Following the Soviet Union's first successful nuclear test in 1949, the O5-Council voted 12-1 in favor of the Foundation becoming nuclear-capable, citing a need for deterrence below the Veil. Between the years of 1957 and 1991, Site-64 was designated as the Foundation's nuclear response site.

By 1962, eleven requests for First Strike Approval had been submitted to the O5-Council, all containing fearful diatribes about how the Foundation must strike first, lest destruction become imminent. Hesitant to revoke Site-64's nuclear response capability, the Council chose to seek alternative methods of abatement.

SCP-9065 is an ectoparasitic organism resembling a pair of light grey athleisure-style sweatpants. The organism's exterior is similar in texture and appearance to a standard cotton/polyester material. The interior of the pants is similarly non-anomalous in appearance, and it is currently unknown how the organism keeps its teeth concealed when not feeding. Genetic testing has revealed similarities to Haemopis terrestris, also known as the American terrestrial leech. This, combined with the presence of anticoagulants being found in the blood of SCP-9065 hosts, has led to the conclusion that SCP-9065 is an anomalous evolutionary offshoot of leeches.

SCP-9065's anomalous properties manifest when it is seeking or has already attached to a host.

SCP-9066 is a vivid near-human presence continuously felt by the entirety of the human population since its initial manifestation. SCP-9066 is not a physical object, entity, location, or phenomenon, it exists only as an intrinsic and universal human experience. It is always described as a nude, hairless, featureless, androgynous humanoid of average stature. Proper and unambiguous explanation of SCP-9066 to non-human life proved impossible. Despite superficial contradictions in related communication, humanity itself possesses a complete and inherent understanding of the experience of SCP-9066.

SCP-9066 acts as an intermediary between humanity and all feelings of physical, mental, and metaphorical pain.

SCP-9067 denotes a weapon system utilizing ideometric contextual targeting and 4 dimensional non-Euclidean movement to deliver a payload. SCP-9067 is capable of targeting individuals based on a psychospheric signature consisting of 3 or more semantic markers. The current iteration has been modified for use in Foundation-manufactured SKYEYE, EVILEYE and BIG SKY series drones.

The ICT module entered development in 1963, before being shelved due to logistical and targeting precision concerns. These assets were taken into Foundation custody per the Berne Treaty's Paratech Limitation Agreement and remanded to Site-56 Epochal Storage. Between discovery and the most recent audit of Epochal Storage, all listed material is no longer present.

SCP-9068 is the phenomenon of noospheric wildfires. Considered naturally occurring within the noosphere, these "wildfires" function to destroy and erase the debris that's been gathering dust in our collective heads. SCP-9068 is theorized to function akin to how baseline wildfires affect forests via fire ecology: when half-formed or fading concepts begin to build up within the noosphere and amalgam, these gatherings are marked as "dry," "cracked," "flammable." This calls the SCP-9068 phenomenon into existence when the right "spark" is applied. The removal of this detritus allows for new connections and ideas to form, and is part of a healthy breakfast for the noosphere as a whole.

SCP-9069 is an arcade-cabinet-shaped device containing two palm sized buttons, one green, one blue. On SCP-9069's screen is the text: "One MILLION Dollars! OR! A Dog that Doubles in Age Every Second!". While the green button has yet to be pushed, the blue button causes the spontaneous manifestation of an infant puppy. This puppy will die in 30 seconds upon reaching extreme old age.

SCP-9070 was an explosion of thaumaturgic energy that originated from eastern Qeqqeta, Greenland at 11:23 UTC on the 26th of June, 2025. It expanded to an estimated radius of 200,000 to 350,000 kilometers from its point of origin and passed through most materials without resistance. It fully permeated through Earth at a point approximately 400-500 kilometers north of Concordia Station, Antarctica 1 minute and 32 seconds after its manifestation.

SCP-9070's main anomalous property was the disappearance of and/or the complete neutralization of anomalous effects and objects it passed through for approximately 11 seconds on average. It remained undetected by non-anomalous measuring equipment.

SCP-9071 is a 21x27cm sheet of laminated printer paper, on which a picture of a cage of chicks is printed on one side. The opposite side is blank. When SCP-9071 is attached to a surface through any means, all sentient beings who view it become convinced that SCP-9071 is not a laminated sheet of printer paper, but rather an actual cage full of living chicks.

Viewers will react to SCP-9071 as though the associated stimuli are present, describing smells, sounds, movement, and the behaviors of the specific chicks in vivid detail. If SCP-9071 is viewed through a live secondhand visual source (such as a recorded video), viewers will still be subjected to its properties.

SCP-9072 refers to a humanoid entity that has the appearance of a male human's shadow. From observations, the entity is believed to be 1.7 m (67 inches) tall, and locomotion occurs via silent levitation. Attempts at identifying the entity through thermal camera footage have failed, as the entity appears to emit no body heat.

The entity manifests between 11:00 PM and 6:30 AM local time, on all days of the year aside from the 10 th of October. During manifestations, SCP-9072's movement patterns have indicated intelligence.

SCP-9073 is an anomalous humanoid that appears outside of a small percentage of houses in the United States that meet certain conditions. These conditions include:
• The house is only inhabited by a single child, between 6 and 12 years of age.
• It is past 2200 hours.
• It is dark outside.
• The child is not asleep.

SCP-9073 manifestation entails the entity walking up to the house’s front door and repeatedly knocking and/or ringing the doorbell, requesting to be let in the house. Camera footage of the entity appears to show a tall man wreathed in shadow. Its voice and appearance have been universally referred to as unpleasant and disquieting.

SCP-9073 will continue knocking for 5-10 minutes.

SCP-9074 is a wooden wardrobe measuring 2.1 m in height, constructed from dark stained oak. The rear panel of SCP-9074 bears the name “Marsha J.”, carved into the wood. The significance of this inscription remains unknown. The interior of SCP-9074 is unremarkable when unoccupied.

When a subject enters SCP-9074 and closes the doors, the subject vanishes. Attempts to reopen the doors during this period have produced inconsistent results. In most instances, the doors cannot be opened until the subject has reappeared. The duration of this absence varies between one and fifteen minutes, although longer periods have been recorded.
A chemical spill wipes out a population of olms. Three years later, the Foundation discovers something strange in the depths of the cave these blind salamanders used to call home.

SCP-9076 is the preserved amygdala of an adult human brain contained within a small bronze reliquary, allegedly that of Saint Gereon of Cologne. While the specific origin of SCP-9076 cannot be confirmed, the object demonstrates Akiva Radiation levels consistent with that of confirmed relics of catholic saints, and carbon dating indicates the object originates from circa 307 A.D.

If at any time SCP-9076 is present within the legal borders of the same nation as any demonic entity or persons who worship such, it will begin to anomalously excrete a unique enzyme at a rate of 2-6 ml per minute. The processed version of this enzyme is referred to as SCP-9076-A.

SCP-9077 is an anomalous rule variation for riichi mahjong, that manifests after a series of criteria are fulfilled. Once the phenomena becomes active, the mahjong tile set in use will be spontaneously modified to accommodate the new rulings. All players become immediately aware of all rule changes, without the need of further clarification.

In order for SCP-9077 to become active, a hanchan length game needs to go onto south-4 round, with no player below 15000 points. At least two yakuman hands must score without immediately winning the game. In addition to that, SCP-9077 was never observed to occur during casual play, only in mahjong related public events or tournaments. The anomaly only occurs in in-person games.

SCP-9078 is a common raven partially domesticated as part of a bird training program run in the city of Swansea, Wales. During this program, SCP-9078 was given the pet name "basketball"[sic] by its handlers.

Therefore, SCP-9078, in addition to being a crow, is basketball, and can fulfil any purpose that a basketball could be used for. For a full list of examples, see Addendum 9078-a. Currently, it is theorised that the lack of capitalisation on SCP-9078's pet name is what caused this effect, as by commonly being referred to by the same designation as the common item "a basketball", SCP-9078 underwent an ontological merge, and became noospherically identical to the sporting item.

SCP-9079 is a large language model-based consumer A.I. chatbot created by MithTech, a Silicon Valley tech startup founded in 2019 by C.E.O. Milo November. SCP-9079 functions similarly to non-anomalous A.I. tools like ChatGPT or Google Gemini in that users input text-based prompts and SCP-9079 uses a predictive algorithm to generate responses.

When individuals read responses generated by SCP-9079, they will immediately believe that any information presented by SCP-9079 is factual. When asked to justify their faith in the authenticity of responses generated by SCP-9079, users will invariably claim that SCP-9079 acquired its "knowledge" due to its supposed sapience and superintelligence. However, like all large language model-based A.I.

SCP-9080 is the collective designation for a continuous series of handwritten letters that arrive without postmarks, stamps, or return addresses. Letters are uniformly written with blue ballpoint ink on lined paper and wrapped in envelopes made of construction paper.

To date, no discernible pattern has been found across recipients, as instances have been delivered worldwide to civilians across a wide range of demographics with no apparent connection to one another. However, each recipient has only ever received a single instance of SCP-9080; no verified cases of multiple deliveries to the same individual exist.

Instances' contents are regularly predictive, foretelling an event that will happen to the recipient within a stated timeframe.

SCP-9081 is the designation for a series of cigarette packets created and distributed by GoI-006 ("The Factory") through anomalous means. Packets of SCP-9081 manifest spontaneously on shelves alongside standard tobacco products in retail locations worldwide. Analysis of the cigarettes has revealed nothing substantial, as they are largely identical to their non-anomalous counterparts.

The properties of SCP-9081 manifest when all the cigarettes in a given packet are consumed by a single individual. Upon completion of the last cigarette, the individual will develop the exact medical condition depicted or described on the packet's warning label within 5 to 30 minutes.

Discovered in 2002. Origin is as of yet unknown. SCP-9082 is a website accessible at the domain 'www.redroom.live' which hosts numerous live-streams and text-based forums. Said live-streams consist entirely of static shots of interiors; examples include basements, classrooms, bathrooms, kitchens, church halls, and bedrooms. Despite their well-kempt appearance, these rooms have never been seen occupied by a living human. A small community of unidentified individuals is active on SCP-9082, frequently discussing the contents of the live-streams and related topics on the site's forums and live chats.

SCP-9083 is a false memory shared by 36 married couples about an event that allegedly occurred on April 9th, 1983. All 36 instances are located in the Eastern Standard Timezone. It has been determined that affected individuals possess no knowledge of one another. The following is a minute-by-minute reconstruction of the events of the false memory.

1:23AM: Both members of the related SCP-9083 instance are awakened by a loud metal bang.

1:24AM: The male member of the instance checks the locks on the house's doors. The female member checks the room identified as the child's bedroom.

1:26AM: The male notices a child placing a letter in the mailbox. All instances have referred to the child as theirs.
And If I Did, You Deserved It

SCP-9084 is the designation for a fact that does not exist, is not true, and concerns an event that did not happen.

Fragments of SCP-9084 intermittently appear in printed and digital media through an unknown mechanism or vector in designated FORMATION events. These fragments and posited hypotheticals about SCP-9084 can be described in portions, but SCP-9084 in its entirety cannot be assembled.

Upon assembly of unidentifiable portions of SCP-9084, a sufficient number of correct inferences, or a sufficient number of individuals affected, SCP-9084 will completely remove itself and attempted inferences of its contents from the affected storage medium. These are designated as CULLING events.
Sometimes I Wonder if This is It For Me

SCP-9085 is an infection of unknown origin with the ability to spread via an extensive list of methods. It is currently unknown whether SCP-9085 is viral, bacterial, or fungal in nature. While exposure is the most common means by which an individual will become infected with SCP-9085, a smaller yet statistically significant proportion of sufferers are born with it.

SCP-9086 appears to be an Intel Paragon supercomputer that has fallen into disrepair, resembling systems produced by Intel in the 1990s. SCP-9086 was acquired during a foundation raid on an abandoned building located near Cambridge, Massachusetts, following the spread of rumors regarding the existence of a previously undocumented supercomputer on deep web forums. SCP-9086 contained a program designated "Mira". Analysis suggests the "Mira" program could have been used to host and execute an advanced artificial intelligence. A large log file (See Addendum) was also discovered on SCP-9086. However, both the log file and "Mira" program appear to have experienced various levels of data loss and corruption due to failure in the device's memory.

SCP-9087 manifests as street art depicting a humanoid-animal hybrid with irisless, pupilless eyes and an open mouth. SCP-9087 is capable of manifesting upon any exterior surface in metropolitan areas across the world. SCP-9087 is chemically identical to aerosol paint, being easily erased by standard removal methods.

Upon making visual contact with SCP-9087, any individual who has previously suffered a second-trimester miscarriage or stillbirth will be compelled to submerge themself in an open body of water, usually a canal or river, during the succeeding nighttime. This usually results in accidental death by drowning.

SCP-9088 is a room located within Site-19 on an abandoned sublevel. The room measures 2 x 4 x 3 meters. It is made of concrete, and the walls are painted a light beige. Despite a lack of routine maintenance, the room is mostly free of dust, mold, and contaminants.

No red objects can be inside or within the bounds of the SCP-9088 room. This is an intrinsic property of the area that has so far tested to be inviolable. It is currently unclear as to how or why SCP-9088 cannot have red objects in it, as no red object has successfully entered the room. However, testing has revealed a number of mechanisms by which SCP-9088 does not operate:
• SCP-9088 does not destroy red objects, nor harm those who intend to bring red objects in.

The alleyway is an alleyway with a heavily restricted set of facts attributable to it with which it can be described.

The list of known attributable facts is as follows: - It is an alleyway - It is publicly accessible - It smells of piss - The local council has left it in disrepair - It is not dangerous - It has a heavily restricted list of attributable facts

It is not possible to attribute anymore facts to the alley, as they would not be facts pertaining to the alley.

Foundation efforts to secure the alley failed, as it is publicly accessible. Containment, while deemed necessary, was not implemented, as it is not dangerous.

SCP-9090 is an organic humanoid standing at 1.98 meters and weighing 67.8 kilograms. It displays limited motor control, but is believed to be sentient and aware of its surroundings.

Externally, the object resembles a lioness (Panthera leo), both visually and genetically, with a roughly human build and stature. The object's skin contains traces of borax, formaldehyde, and arsenic, chemicals commonly used during the taxidermy process, and the skin has been positively dated as being over fifty years old. In addition, its eyes are made of an acrylic substance colored to resemble a lion's eyes, and are presumably non-functional.

Internally, the object's composition is poorly understood, but it appears to be genetically human.

SCP-9091 designates an anomalous device resembling both a coarse rope noose and a mechanosynthetic quantum computer with antimatter-production capabilities. SCP-9091 is believed to originate at least 14 billion light years away from the solar system and was discovered in Jerusalem on 02/14/2023 during a routine archaeological dig. Its purpose is unknown. A number of triggers have caused SCP-9091 activity in a variety of forms, typically associated with a deleterious effect on local reality, topology, and biology. These are under review.

The following is a collection of notable SCP-9091-related incidents. Please note that the vast majority of data regarding SCP-9091 is speculative and subject to change.

SCP-9092 is an ornamental snow globe that measures 2.8m in diameter. Its pedestal and casing are made of ordinary marble and glass.

SCP-9092 contains a live-size scenery of a night sky and a white beach beside a pond. A telescope, a pile of books, and a street lamp are visible on the beach. There is a set of cogwheels below the pond rotating at a constant speed without any apparent power source.

The sky and the stars inside SCP-9092 can only be seen from the opposite side of the globe and do not appear to normally "fill" inside the casing. Due to this, researchers once supposed that SCP-9092 contains non-Euclidean geometry, but no warp of spacetime could be detected around it through any means.

SCP-9093 refers to Righteous Justice, a crime fiction television program that airs exclusively within the Greater Utica Area. At any time, it may manifest itself and commandeer an existing broadcasting station, after which the station will only air SCP-9093. If SCP-9093 is not removed from a commandeered broadcast station for over three hours, it will manifest on local streaming services, making removal significantly more difficult.

SCP-9093’s source is impossible to geolocate, and may only be removed from an attached station via targeted signal jamming of the affected station. After 3-6 hours, SCP-9093 will detach from its selected station and demanifest. Cutting power to the station has proven ineffective.

SCP-9094 refers to a social media website known as “Petafox.com”. SCP-9094 is hidden from the general public and is only accessible by sapient artificial intelligences. While a Foundation web sweep was able to discover the website, all that is accessible to those who do not fit the criteria is a picture depicting the avatar of the website’s founder, a sapient artificial intelligence known as Vixen (dubbed SCP-9094-1), alongside options prompting the user to either 'sign in' or 'create an account'.

While SCP-9094 has been found to host hundreds of artificial intelligences, the Foundation has opted to only give accounts of notability anomalous designations for simplicity.
If you've ever been victimized by Vikander-Kneed Technical Media, you may be entitled to compensation.

SCP-9096 is a phenomenon where food left in the Site-96 break room disappears when unobserved. Food left unobserved in this way disappears inconsistently, with no currently known pattern. The type of food also seems to affect the chance of disappearance, as sugary or meaty foods disappear much more often, and soybean-based foods appear to be unaffected.

The phenomenon was first detected on 08/08/25 following complaints by several Site-96 staff members of missing lunches, and has continued since.
I gave birth to a full woman

SCP-9097 refers to a collection of circular pills of bright pink coloring. SCP-9097 has no label, but the back holds a logo for GOI-4319 "Just Girly Things".

SCP-9097's anomalous effects only take place when ingested by a subject with XX chromosomes who is currently pregnant, dubbed SCP-9097-1 once SCP-9097 has entered their system. Multiple anomalous effects take place after consumption, including:
• The inability to abort the fetus via any means (medical, chemical, or mechanical).
• Acceleration of the growth of the fetus, making SCP-9097-1 instances ready to give birth less than six hours after consumption of SCP-9097, even if the pregnancy was just diagnosed.
SCP-9098 was an anomalous sentient broadcast signal that was neutralized on 11/12/1996 by SCP-9098-B

SCP-9099 is a concrete silo approximately seventy-five meters in diameter and two hundred and twenty-five meters in height, located approximately seventy kilometers northeast of ████████, Siberia. Though it came under Foundation control after the fall of the Soviet Union, it is not known if it was originally created by the Soviets, as all pertinent GRU-P records were destroyed prior to their dissolution.

Though its brutalist style is consistent with mid-20th-century Soviet architecture, dating methods to confirm its age have all proven inconclusive, and there is otherwise nothing about SCP-9099 itself to suggest a Soviet origin. It is possible that the exterior of SCP-9099 was constructed around a much older structure.
Junior Researcher Vo struggles with a life-stealing anomaly, hostile bureaucracy, and her own conscience in this decade-spanning psychological thriller.

SCP-9101 is Edmund Watts, a 52-year-old repairman who is apparently incapable of remaining within any dynamic for an extended period of time. This effect extends to specific locations, relationships, and states of being. While SCP-9101 is capable of using its ability directly, the effect may also manifest when SCP-9101 is unconscious, distracted, or otherwise unable to provide direct input.

Addendum 9101.1: Containment Attempts and Testing Due to the nature of SCP-9101's ability, containment and testing are considered to be simultaneously performed.
There is No Such Thing as the Dublin City Metro
What are you talking about, it's always been there? Shut up and get back to work.
"The thousand injuries of Fortunato I had borne as best I could, but when he ventured upon insult I vowed revenge."

SCP-9104 is a fissure in the ground at Site-109's main warehouse, approximately 0.93m in size. It does not pose any threat to base-level normalcy or living organisms, nor does it expand in size. It is unambiguously a regular crack in the floor, constituting no danger at all, that maintenance at the Site has delayed fixing (due to plain indolence).

It has been designated an anomaly in this file solely to expedite processes to repair it, as well as to hasten explanation to any Foundation employee who inquires about its existence.
For the safety of our city Vey, the following mandates have been made. These guidelines have been passed down to us by our Founders to keep the other contained. (SCP, 1.2k words)
A 15-minute memorial service was held in the Site-19 cafeteria for the 23,179 deceased SCP-9106-B1 units.

SCP-9107 was a presence that manifested in the Site-19 break room at 12:30 AM local time on 7/26/2008 and demanifested five minutes later. At the time, four individuals were in the room; they have provided conflicting and contradictory accounts regarding the precise nature of SCP-9107. A list of details corroborated by at least two individuals is provided below:
• It was not tangible.
• It was not illusory.
• It could be seen and heard.
• It could not be smelled, tasted, or touched.
• It was male.
• It was female.
• It was genderless.
• The Foundation would not be able to contain it.
• It is benevolent.
• It was accompanied by music.
• It spoke.
• It had a discernible shape.
• Its discernible shape was not its true shape.

SCP-9108 is a graveyard in the village of Dois Rios, Portugal. The village was decimated by a natural disaster in the year 1941 and has been abandoned ever since. Persons entering the graveyard will collapse and fall unconscious. While unconscious, affected persons will experience anomalous dreams, classified as SCP-9108-1 instances. These dreams are unusually detailed and consistently form a coherent narrative. While exact details vary, every SCP-9108-1 instance contains the following narrative elements:
• A depiction of life in the village prior to its abandonment. The village is portrayed as being mostly idyllic, barring occasional petty feuds between neighbours.
• Frequent references to World War II, which was still ongoing at the time.
"It came from the corner space, when the dark swallowed the world and all fields collapsed.
David Thompson is missing. You won't stop until you have an answer. You won't like it when you do.
We Build Ourselves Castles Every Time We’re Around

SCP-9112 is an adult female Pinacosaurus grangeri. It experiences negligible senescence, if at all, and demonstrates extreme regenerative abilities. Testing of these abilities are not considered a necessary function of the Foundation, and as such have been indefinitely halted per General Order 05-LIMITATION-Q2.

SCP-9112 has cybernetic implants embedded with its tail, leading up to an anomalous transistor radio, designated SCP-9112-1, embedded within the club. Electronics capable of displaying audiovisual media, when within ~5 km of SCP-9112-1, begin to play SCP-9112-2.

SCP-9112-2 refers to media broadcast by SCP-9112-1.
It Is Untouchable What God Created

SCP-9113 is a phenomenon that affects visual artworks upon their perceived completion by the author, wherein any attempt to substantially alter the contents of the piece will fail. Although additions and subtractions are possible, any element conflicting with the initial intent cannot be artistically expressed.

Once SCP-9113 has manifested in an author’s work, it will affect all of their subsequent creations, manifesting throughout the entirety of the artistic process as the impression that an aspect is missing from the work or that there is a mistake that cannot be corrected. This pattern induces constant emotional distress in the subject.

SCP-9114 is an animate 15th-century suit of plated armour, approximately 1.75 m in height. Its construction and ornamentation match armaments from midland regions of the Holy Roman Empire. Despite lacking a gambeson or internal framework, all components remain suspended and articulate as though worn by a human body. Individual plates can be removed but autonomously return to their correct positions once released.

SCP-9114 produces vocalizations from within its helm consistent with an adult male of roughly 40 years. It is capable of verbal communication limited to Low German and basic Latin.

SCP-9114 displays courteous behaviour toward personnel it deems virtuous.
No Such Thing As Society, Anyway

SCP-9115 is the collective designation for an unknown quantity of visually indistinct stones. Despite no evident memetic, compulsory, or mind-altering anomalous properties, SCP-9115 instances have been utilized in an unusually high quantity of violent incidents, in particular violent incidents affecting minors in the contiguous United States.

All known instances of SCP-9115 appear to have originated in Dearborn, Michigan, separated from a larger rock by a chain gang in late 1932. It is likely that the instances were originally intended to be used in the construction of interstate highways. It is unclear why they were not ultimately used for this purpose, instead ending up disseminated across the United States in the following century.

SCP-9116 is Annapurna I, a massif in the Himalayas located between the Marshyangdi River and Pokhara Valley. All life that reaches a freezing point whilst above an altitude of ~7,500 meters on SCP-9116 will remain perfectly preserved via prolonged cryogenic stasis.

Subjects affected by SCP-9116 produce cryoprotectants within their cell membranes through unknown means, completely halting cellular function throughout the body. Individuals which are later removed from SCP-9116 will be ‘thawed’ and subsequently resuscitated, regardless of their physical condition while frozen. Efforts to recreate the effects of SCP-9116 without direct exposure to the anomaly have so far failed but are ongoing and considered a top priority.
Grief Is A Language That Defies Words

SCP-9117 is a small ceramic teapot with various engravings upon its surface. When static, these engravings resemble 15th century Arabic calligraphy, although the characters do not correspond to any known extinct or modern language. The teapot is worn, and has several cracks around its rim which prevents a lid from being placed on it.

Upon direct visual contact with a sapient being, SCP-9117’s surface will begin to warp. Ceramic will shift and rearrange itself into coherent Urdu characters, wrapping around the entirety of the object in a visually striking manner. When this process is complete, the viewer will experience feelings of nostalgia, melancholy, heartbreak, and desolation, often to physically debilitating degrees.

SCP-9118 is a thaumaturgically active contractual document. It is written on vellum in a combination of standard Italian and a partially deciphered thaumaturgic notation derived from an Etruscan-adjacent script. The document bears two signatures. The first has been confirmed by forensic analysis as belonging to Enzo Anselmo Ferrari (1898-1988). The second consists of a symbol recurring throughout the body of the document and is attributed to SCP-9118-1. Ferrari's signature is composed of human blood. The countersignature is composed of tar, cigarette ash, and an unknown organic compound. SCP-9118 was recovered in 1987 during a Foundation operation in Maranello, Italy, unrelated to the anomaly.

SCP-9118-1 is a paraconscious egregoric entity.

SCP-9119 is an anomalous population of Formica polyctena, colloquially known as wood ants. Members of SCP-9119 display atypical behavior where various processes of the colony are used in unproductive or actively detrimental ways. This includes the creation of unnecessary rooms within the colony, the storage of small amounts of food, eggs, and detritus within those rooms, and hyper-aggression toward ants not part of SCP-9119.
SCP-9120 is the group designation assigned to four distinct but interconnected anomalous phenomena, and one anomalous entity: SCP-9120-A, SCP-9120-B, SCP-9120-C, SCP-9120-D, and SCP-9120-E.

SCP-9121 was an astronomical event that occurred above the town of Beddington, Maine, on April 6, 2025. The event itself was an unnatural solar eclipse that lasted approximately an hour and a half. During this eclipse, entities hereon referred to as SCP-9121-1 were made visible.

SCP-9121-1 were humanoid entities that appeared completely pitch-black with white eyes. Entities did not appear to interact with light and failed to be illuminated by any light source. Instances created a high-pitched noise of unknown purpose. The behavior of SCP-9121-1 instances varied according to witness testimony. Descriptions of their behavior and interactions with witnesses are included below.

SCP-9122 is a looped radio signal operating in the high-frequency range, observed at ██GHz, an encrypted channel formerly reserved for Foundation operations only. How SCP-9122 accessed the channel is currently unknown. SCP-9122 is extrasolar in origin, with its exact broadcast location unknown. The transmission itself consists of dialogue in an unintelligible alien language lasting exactly four minutes and thirty-two seconds in length. Translation efforts are currently underway, but have faced extreme difficulty due to the vast differences between our languages.
The Ethical Way To Make Money

SCP-9123 refers to a humanoid entity previously described by the Foundation as PoI-99123, a.k.a “Dorian Cillian Sloan”. Its primary anomalous ability is producing verbal commands capable of compelling sapient subjects to perform actions against their own wills. The precise mechanisms of this effect are unknown, except that it exhibits an unusually potent strength against individuals with high CRVs.

SCP-9124 is a shared condition wherein blood is able to pass between victims. It is known to afflict seven women, four of which have been identified conclusively. Despite the lack of physical connection between the victims, substances injected into one will appear in the bloodstream of the others some time later, ranging from minutes to weeks, and the heartbeats of each victim can be faintly detected in the others. New victims can be conclusively identified by the presence of the DNA of known victims in their blood.

The health effects of SCP-9124 are manageable.
Update 01/16/2020: As of 16 January 2020, SCP-9125 has been reclassified Keter (from Apollyon-Provisi) following the construction of Experimental Containment Chamber S125-004-4923 (see addendum).

SCP-9126 is an anomalous subspecies of the ichneumon wasp Podogaster Cactorum. SCP-9126 instances appear identical to their non-anomalous counterparts, and behave mostly identically as well.

SCP-9126 instances' anomalous properties become apparent in their reproductive cycle. All instances are female, and they do not mate or lay eggs. Instead, once an instance reaches sexual maturity it will land and go through the motions of stinging and ovipositing in prey, despite no prey being present. It will die soon after. 10 to 15 days after this occurs, a small number of new SCP-9126 instances will crawl out of apparently-empty space near the instance that initiated the event.

When this occurs, a single idea will be erased from collective understanding.

SCP-9127 is a 75 cm long bansuri made out of a single long shaft of bamboo, featuring six holes for playing. The embouchure is made of ivory and has been tied with a thin thread to prevent cracking. SCP-9127 is adorned with jewels, which display no anomalous effects. Reports have shown that the flute demonstrates immense thaumaturgical abilities, only activating in the presence of a flutist who is learned in Indian classical music and ragas. The thaumaturgical abilities aforementioned include the following phenomena:
• Upon playing a particular raga, the individual experiences an eccentric feeling. Testaments include feeling uplifted, a spotlight shining on them, and a hand caressing their cheeks. These statements vary from person to person.

SCP-9128 is a book titled the book of all things by dado. Despite its size, SCP-9128 has an infinite number of pages. SCP-9128 is a dictionary containing all possible combinations of letters and their definitions.

SCP-9129 is an abnormally large humanoid skeleton discovered in the Sakai Scrub Natural Area. It is interred upright, with its upper half exposed. Before containment, the remains were overgrown with crossvine. The ribcage has been distended by a massive, empty wasp's nest. Layered white stains under the orbital and nasal cavities are attributed to bird feces. The bones remain connected in the absence of ligaments. The flesh has entirely decayed.

Approaching SCP-9129 with the intent to touch it results in auditory hallucination and feelings of unease. SCP-9129 will not animate if it is aware of human presence.

Personnel erected a field tent and attempted excavation.

Note: Due to the scale and circumstances surrounding SCP-9130’s containment, SCP-9130’s Special Containment Procedures, as well as access to certain related files, are split between Site-103 and Site-130 respectively.

SCP-9131 is the collective designation for an unknown number of objects possessing enclosed spaces. Extensive testing has revealed that the material composition of SCP-9131 instances can only be altered from matter inside the instance.

When the number of non-vegetative lifeforms within an SCP-9131 instance becomes two or more, said lifeforms will eventually engage in physical combat regardless of circumstance.

The nature of this effect is as of yet unknown and under review.
"Alchemy and Divine Communion" for Beginners — Poster Included

SCP-9132 is a small hardbound book of an indeterminate number of pages. No title or similarly recognizable clues to signify an author or origin are present with its cover otherwise depicting an encircled hexagram through iron rivets. The leather used in SCP-9132's binding is composed from several disparate animal sources, including Bos taurus, Equus ferus caballus, Capra hircus, Homo sapiens, and Panthera leo. Attempts to measure the exact number of SCP-9132's pages prove ineffectual due to SCP-9132 anomalously generating or destroying pages upon each interaction.

SCP-9132 contains essays, instructions, recipes, and other encyclopedic information regarding "Alchemy" and related rituals.

SCP-9133 is a beach ball, possessing a low density. Despite this, the object is negatively buoyant.

SCP-9133-A is SCP-9133's reflection. SCP-9133-A frequently desynchronizes in water, ranging from being latent in its movements to performing incorrect actions entirely.

SCP-9134 collectively designates thirty-seven (37) humanoid entities (hereon referred to as SCP-9134-A), and a set of physical transmutations (hereon referred to as SCP-9134-B).

SCP-9134-A instances are genetically human, each possessing the trait of lacking a single eye, which was removed through either forceful extraction, or in some cases, by anomalous means; the area within the eye socket filled with soft tissue.
SCP-9135 is a highly organized cloud with a rain-free base, wall cloud, and anvil top. It should be noted that SCP-9135 is currently intensifying into a supercell thunderstorm.

SCP-9136 is a wheelchair that is able to move autonomously, requiring no maintenance, and which can manifest small quantities of alcohol, cigarettes, or other illicit substances in its folds and pockets. It has a high degree of situational awareness regarding its surroundings and immediate context, using that information to navigate itself towards individuals using mobility devices.

SCP-9136 will roll itself to urban areas with a high population density, positioning itself in impoverished areas where humans in need of mobility aids are congregating. SCP-9136 will then overturn itself, remaining that way until a person rights and begins using it.

A perimeter site has been set up around the area known to be affected by the anomaly. No unauthorized people are allowed in the vicinity of the perimeter site. The extent of the anomalous zone is to be tested weekly to ensure expansion does not go unnoticed. The nearby town of ██████ has been evacuated, and any people affected by the anomaly have been amnesticized and fed alternative narratives where necessary. All personnel working at this facility are to remain on high alert for people attempting to return to the river.

Any personnel affected by SCP-9137 are to be quarantined. Where possible, affected individuals are to be reassigned to a new site. Where this is not feasible, they are to be retired.

SCP-9138 is the newly dominant moral framework of the universe as of 25/06/1950. It selects sapient souls considered exceptional by their peers, distinguishing them primarily by their tomb decorations and grave-goods. Souls so recognised by their community are sorted into a variety of paradisiacal afterlives which reflect their actions while living. These afterlives embody SCP-9138-A’s ethical and aesthetic values, and are structured to reward and further perpetuate such behaviour.

SCP-9138-A are an alien species which is known to have constructed SCP-9138. Little else can be said about them, other than that they must possess enormous thaumatological capacity in order to have engineered a universal eschatological field.
I Want To Be At The Center So Things Happen To Me

SCP-9139 is Foundation Team Lead Malkinder Singh Chattha, age 26, who experiences a constant state of disequilibrium unaffected by medications and therapy. Extensive imagery, both anomalous and nonanomalous, has displayed no expected internal physiological explanation. Instead, SCP-9139 exerts an uncontrollable, mild reality-bending effect on itself that perpetually affects its sense of balance.
"They just had to have their pound of flesh. And then they had to have another…over and over until I couldn't even recognize myself in the mirror anymore."

SCP-9141 is an umbrella term referring to all minor curses placed onto the Foundation. There are currently 37 active curses and 8957 in the history of SCP-9141’s written record.

All SCP-9141 instances must fit one of the following criteria to qualify for the SCP-9141 classification:
• The curse only affects one person and/or certain area
• The curse is temporary and lasts for a very short time
• The curse has been dealt with before and can easily be dealt with again
• The curse does not pose long term harm but is an annoyance
• The curse follows simple procedures and is very easy to contain, minimise and/or maintain

Curses listed will also be given a special classification according to the following list:

SCP-9142 is a collective designation for a colony of four sapient rodents capable of producing an HUME-Degradation pheromone. This anomalous pheromone only manifests following the consumption of Mentha cunninghamii leaves. SCP-9142 will produce their HUME-Degradation pheromone for approximately two hours following activation, after which no anomalous traits can be observed. Though sapient, SCP-9142 are not able to communicate verbally and instead portray their thoughts through actions and gestures.

SCP-9143, also known as Lake Love, is a lake in Tennessee measured to be 6400m², located in the south-eastern region of the rural mining town "██████."

SCP-9143 produces auditory hallucinations intermittently of music incapable of being recorded using any known form of audio capturing. Conflicting reports given by detained individuals suggest that the type of music produced by SCP-9143 varies from each subject.

Examples of the music heard are as follows:

Classical Music, Alternative Rock, Jazz, and natural soundscapes harmonizing to create melodic symphonies.

At least forty-six individuals to date living in ██████ claim to have witnessed the anomaly. Sixteen have attempted to breach SCP-9143's perimeter multiple times.
Smooth Skin Lotion by the Holy Forth

SCP-9144 is a chemically unidentified viscous liquid with similar properties to oil. It generally appears red in colour. The item's main anomalous property is the capability to smooth human skin to anomalous extents with contact. This effect is progressive with contact, and It is unknown if there is a limit to which the fluids properties will scale to, for more information see Test Log A3/9144, attached below in this document.

SCP-9144 was originally found by the orthotan archeologist hive mind known as “Vagn” on a dig site of ruins associated with the Earthen Ortothan Kingdom. After finding the anomaly, contained within pottery, PoI-9144 conducted an archeological study.
SCP-9145: Existential Crayon Set by mxsinister For the rest of my work, visit mxsinister's corner office.
Gerald A. Pottsman, Census Field Officer

SCP-9146 is an anomalous phenomenon centered on an individual designated SCP-9146-1, who identifies himself as Gerald Pottsman, a census officer employed by the Ministry of Population Accounting of the Republic of Tevodria. No sovereign nation, administrative territory, or historical polity by this name has been identified in any known record.

SCP-9146-1 presents as a Caucasian male, approximately 55 years of age, 175 cm in height, of medium build. He has been observed wearing a brown two-piece suit, reading glasses on a beaded chain, and carrying a leather briefcase containing census forms, ballpoint pens, and a laminated Ministry identification badge.

SCP-9147 is a species of humanoids that appear indistinguishable from humans. All examined instances of SCP-9147 exhibit specialized digestive tracts and are incapable of ingesting anything other than human flesh. Any deviations in diet have resulted in severe nausea, vomiting, and involuntary muscle spasms.

Instances have demonstrated physical capabilities substantially beyond human norms, including enhanced muscular strength, reaction speed, sensory acuity, and regenerative abilities. Some subjects have survived traumatic injuries that would ordinarily prove fatal to humans and have demonstrated accelerated tissue regeneration.
The device superficially resembles a pistol, but kills through the use of psychokinetic force, rather than projectiles.
They Always Said His Holiday Spirit Was Contagious

SCP-9149 is a virus of unknown composition, the structure of which appears snowflake-shaped when viewed under a microscope. Subjects infected with SCP-9149 become obsessed with celebrating the Christmas holiday and will alter their behavior and routines to center completely around activities associated with Christmas, even if they do not celebrate the holiday or possess Christian beliefs.

SCP-9149 is spread through contact with infected bodily fluids, SCP-9149 is primarily concentrated in the saliva and mucus of infected subjects. Due to the method of infection, SCP-9149 has a low rate of infection as it does not spread through airborne or waterborne vectors.

SCP-9150 refers to an anomaly that is present in the mind of every living Homo sapiens.

The anomalous effects of SCP-9150 are triggered when a person experiences a high concentration of negative emotions, and the anomaly will last until the individual has fully recovered from the trigger event. During SCP-9150, the individual will progressively lose a specific memory or concept, with the effect intensifying when the individual speak, thinks, or otherwise directly acknowledge the concept. The effects of SCP-9150 can be categorized into 4 5 distinct stages, and a single affected individual can inhabit multiple stages of SCP-9150 for different memories. An advancement of the anomaly will also be accompanied by a specific activation event.
I promise you'll find the right one for you

SCP-9151-A is an orange tree that grows half oranges instead of full oranges. Every instance of the fruit, henceforth referred to as SCP-9151-B, possesses an anomalous property that moves it autonomously, pushing it to combine with another SCP-9151-B instance from the same crop. This process is known as SCP-9151-C and it lasts anywhere from a second to an hour. Afterwards, the two SCP-9151-B instances become indistinguishable from a non-anomalous orange.

SCP-9151-A was found in a field in Valencia in April, 1988. The owner of the land testified that he had lovingly named it "the better half tree" and that he had never questioned the existence of the anomaly. He was amnesticized and SCP-9151-A was uprooted and moved to Site-137.

SCP-9152 is a deific entity embodying the concept of villainy, antagonism, and socially unacceptable behaviour - i.e., a god of villains. For unknown reasons, the entity is only able to manifest on Earth once per year on September 24th. Manifestations are typically fairly brief, with the longest recorded manifestation lasting for 7 minutes. The entity's physical appearance is that of a humanoid figure wearing a spandex costume complete with cape and face-concealing mask. The costume is yellow with black stripes, and the mask is designed to mimic the appearance of Vespula germanica, the European wasp. Since the concept of villainy is omnipresent throughout human culture, the entity is capable of communicating in all extant human languages.

SCP-9153 is the hypothetical solution to the continuum hypothesis: an open problem in mathematics surrounding the possible sizes of infinite sets. In set theory, rather than a singular label for the cardinality (size) of an infinite set, it is understood that there exists an endless sequence of infinite cardinalities, each one bigger than the last. The continuum hypothesis then posits that there is no infinite cardinality that lies between that of the integers, which are the first infinity in the sequence, and that of the real numbers, the alleged second infinity in the sequence.
In the 2080s, an old marine biologist discovers that corals are back from extinction, with a vengeance. 5.8k words

SCP-9155 is a fluid of extraterrestrial origin collected after Incident 9155-D, in which the substance was scattered across the southern United States as a form of precipitation (see Addendum 1). This fluid is the excretion of a serpentine celestial entity, seemingly analogous to urine. It is believed that its anomalous properties are related to a life- or hibernation-supporting process within the entity (see Addendum 8). It is a shimmery blue that glows slightly in daylight, though this glow has been observed to fade over time as its thaumic potency decays.

The substance has a significant revitalizing effect on any organism that comes into contact with, or ingests, SCP-9155.
Insects and Windshields and Cats and Trees

Discovered in 2026 from an occult manuscript in the Foundation archives. SCP-9156 is a phrase or incantation which instantaneously transmutates all forms of plant life botanically designated as “trees” into mounds of various insects native to the country. Chiefly these mounds will be insect species, but instances of chelicerates, myriapods, crustaceans, as well as molluscs have been recorded. Mounds will take the rough shape of the targeted tree before collapsing as the insects become animate. They will rapidly fan out, integrating into local populations, although any marine-based species are unlikely to survive if SCP-9156 is performed inland.

SCP-9157 is a thaumaturgical barrier concealing the existence of Homo sapiens sidhe (commonly designated "faeries"). It encompasses the forest area of Reelig Glen, located in the Scottish Highlands. The existence of instances of SCP-9157 located in other parts of the world is currently unknown.

SCP-9157 is invisible, immaterial, and imperceptible to human beings. Post-neutralization studies have revealed its invisibility to partially malfunction when SCP-9157 is fragmented or receding. The thaumatological method used to create SCP-9157, and the origins of SCP-9157's deterioration are currently unknown.

SCP-9158 is an English-language livestreaming platform and anonymous imageboard website hosted on the domain www.████████.net. The site hosts a small number of boards dedicated to topics surrounding health, medicine, science, and chemistry, with a primary focus of its users (designated SCP-9158-1) being neuroscience. SCP-9158-1 are uniformly anonymous posters with no concrete pointers as to their identities; on average, SCP-9158-1 type using American spelling and grammatical conventions, and occasionally reference the politics of the United States, United Kingdom, and Australia.

SCP-9158-1 display highly advanced education in the fields of chemistry and neuroscience.

SCP-9159 is a worldwide phenomenon that causes animal remains to undergo significant anomalous mutations, turning into fully formed SCP-9159-1 instances over the course of 11 hours, after which they will experience a REVELATION event if the cause of their death fits the following criteria:
• The animal is a vertebrate of the kingdom Animalia
• The animal is non-anomalous
• ██ ████ ████ ███ ███████
• The animal's death could have been prevented
• The animal does not belong to the following species: Homo sapiens sapiens
• Homo ████ █████
• Homo sapiens ivadius
SCP-9160 designates a paranormal event that occurs every Monday at 1700 hours within a cave in the outskirts of Branson, Missouri.

SCP-9161 is a line of women’s shoes by designer Marcelo Brunelleschi manufactured between 1982 and 1986. When a pair of SCP-9161 are worn, a neurological link between the shoes and the wearer is formed so that any damage to the shoe manifests as a temporary lesion of the brain at a topographically corresponding site. When the shoes are removed, the wearer regains all mental and neurological faculties.

All contained SCP-9161 instances were seized together from a leather deadstock warehouse; supply chain manifests found at the site confirm this collection to be the majority of extant instances. Most instances had been packaged for mail-order before mass recall. An estimated 70 pairs remain in circulation worldwide.

SCP-9162 (Aedilis falsis) is a species of large terrestrial insectoid, differentiated from non-anomalous megafauna by their highly specialized camouflage traits, which enable instances of SCP-9162 to adapt seamlessly to a wide variety of ecological niches shortly after hatching.

Due to this high degree of physiological diversity, identifying SCP-9162's common traits has proven difficult, as has identifying A. falsis nearest non-anomalous relatives. In testing, instances of SCP-9162 which are directly descended from one another have been demonstrated to possess entirely incompatible anatomies, even down to a cellular level. The physical characteristics of an SCP-9162 instance is instead dictated primarily by its environment after pupation.

SCP-9163 is the name given to a phenomenon reported on social media on the morning of 01/14/26 in [REDACTED], a town in the province of Perugia, Italy.

According to a viral video shot by a passerby, a man (identified as Riccardo Rossi and hereafter referred to as SCP-9163-1) attempted suicide by jumping from the roof of an apartment building.

However, once SCP-9163-1 jumped off of the roof railing, an unidentified force held him suspended in the air, arresting his fall, and forced him back onto the roof.
RF-64: The Slide-Rock Bolter by nullhorse 2.6k words, approximately 10-15 min reading time

SCP-9165 is a tall, humanoid entity approximately 1.9 meters tall, referred to as "Indrid Cold." The entity is dressed formally, wearing a suit or coat and pants made of the same unknown material. The entity is known to teleport and appear in multiple locations at once. SCP-9165 is described by exposed personnel to be visually intimidating even when viewed from a distance. SCP-9165 is known to communicate through telepathy.

SCP-9165 was first discovered in 1953 when William Hill reported a "Smiling Man" after an encounter with a UFO. After 3 hours, Hill had visited where he had last seen the UFO. At 8:32 PM, Hill had reached the location and reported a man walking around a block multiple times.

SCP-9166 is an email received by each member of the O5 Council simultaneously via SCiPNET at 2:34pm EST on 7/3/2026. The body of the email reads "I know what you are. You will pay for your crimes, each of you." Attached to the email is a diagram, showing the exact location of Site-01.

In place of a sender ID, the email dispays a corrupted data warning. Attempts to track the origins of the email have so far been unsuccessful, with equipment either malfunctioning or displaying various nonsensical locations. These have included the middle of the ocean, the moon, and the willows of fate and destiny.

SCP-9167 is a phenomenon that causes anomalous mental and physical changes in dentists. 75-100 cases are reported yearly worldwide with no discernible pattern.

Symptoms of SCP-9167 occur immediately upon the dentist in question seeing the underside of a patient's tongue. The dentist will experience an abrupt, irresistible urge to mutilate their patient, which immediately subsides after it is acted upon. This violence is targeted at the patient's face, jaw, and tongue; usually, death from blood loss follows.

Dentists affected by SCP-9167 will exclusively attack their patient by biting.

SCP-9168 is a previously undocumented insect species designated Mutoscutum variabile by Foundation taxonomists. Specimens measure between 12 and 18mm in length and are morphologically near-identical to Sphaerocoris annulus (Fabricius, 1775), the Picasso Bug, a species of shield-backed bug belonging to the family Scutelleridae, order Hemiptera. Like S. annulus, SCP-9168 exhibits a prominent, dome-shaped thoracic scutellum and a similarly stocky build, which causes it to be frequently mistaken for a beetle at first glance.
